enonce_markdown: A plane passes through the point $(1,2,3)$ and has $2\mathbf i-\mathbf j+4\mathbf k$ as a normal vector. Which is a Cartesian equation of the plane?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A plane with normal $\mathbf n$ through the point with position vector $\mathbf a$ has equation $\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf r=\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf a$.

### Solution

$\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf a=2(1)-1(2)+4(3)=2-2+12=12$. So the plane is $2x-y+4z=12$.

$6$ comes from adding the coordinates of the point, $0$ from assuming the plane passes through the origin, and $-12$ from a sign slip on the right-hand side.

enonce_markdown: The line $\mathbf r=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-\mathbf k+t(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)$ meets the plane $x+2y-z=3$ at the point $T$. What are the coordinates of $T$?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Write the general point of the line in coordinates, substitute into the equation of the plane to get one equation in $t$, then substitute $t$ back.

### Solution

General point: $(1+2t,\ 2-t,\ -1+3t)$. Substituting: $(1+2t)+2(2-t)-(-1+3t)=3$, i.e. $6-3t=3$, so $t=1$ and $T=(3,1,2)$. Check: $3+2-2=3$.

$(1,2,-1)$ is the point $t=0$ (the line's own starting point), $(-1,3,-4)$ is $t=-1$ and $(5,0,5)$ is $t=2$.

enonce_markdown: The planes $\Pi_1:\ x+2y+2z=5$ and $\Pi_2:\ 3x+4z=2$ meet at an acute angle $\theta$. Find $\theta$ to the nearest $0.1^\circ$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The angle between two planes equals the angle between their normals: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{|\mathbf n_1\cdot\mathbf n_2|}{|\mathbf n_1||\mathbf n_2|}$ (taking the modulus gives the acute angle).

### Solution

$\mathbf n_1=(1,2,2)$, $\mathbf n_2=(3,0,4)$. $\mathbf n_1\cdot\mathbf n_2=3+0+8=11$, $|\mathbf n_1|=3$, $|\mathbf n_2|=5$. $\cos\theta=\dfrac{11}{15}$, so $\theta=42.8^\circ$.

$47.2^\circ$ is $90^\circ-\theta$ (used sine), $137.2^\circ$ is the obtuse supplement, and $36.9^\circ$ comes from $\cos\theta=\tfrac45$, using $\mathbf n_2$ only.

enonce_markdown: Find the perpendicular distance from the point $(2,-1,3)$ to the plane $2x-2y+z=4$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The distance from $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ to $ax+by+cz=d$ is $\dfrac{|ax_0+by_0+cz_0-d|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}$.

### Solution

Numerator: $|2(2)-2(-1)+3-4|=|4+2+3-4|=5$. Denominator: $\sqrt{4+4+1}=3$. Distance $=\dfrac53$.

$5$ forgets to divide by $|\mathbf n|$; $\dfrac{13}{3}$ adds $d$ instead of subtracting it; $\dfrac59$ divides by $|\mathbf n|^2$ instead of $|\mathbf n|$.

enonce_markdown: The planes $\Pi_1:\ x+y+z=6$ and $\Pi_2:\ 2x-y+z=3$ meet in a straight line $m$. Find a vector equation of $m$.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The line of intersection is perpendicular to both normals, so its direction is $\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2$. A point on it comes from fixing one coordinate and solving the two equations.

### Solution

$\mathbf n_1\times\mathbf n_2=(1,1,1)\times(2,-1,1)=(1\cdot1-1\cdot(-1),\ 1\cdot2-1\cdot1,\ 1\cdot(-1)-1\cdot2)=(2,1,-3)$.

Put $z=0$: $x+y=6$ and $2x-y=3$, so $3x=9$, $x=3$, $y=3$: the point $(3,3,0)$ lies on both planes.

$m:\ \mathbf r=3\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+t(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)$. Check: direction dot $\mathbf n_1$ is $2+1-3=0$ and dot $\mathbf n_2$ is $4-1-3=0$.

enonce_markdown: Find the coordinates of the foot $F$ of the perpendicular from the point $P(2,3,-1)$ to the plane $2x-y+2z=-10$, and hence the position vector of the image $P'$ of $P$ in this plane.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The perpendicular from $P$ to the plane is the line through $P$ with direction equal to the normal. Its meeting point with the plane is the foot $F$, and the image satisfies $\overrightarrow{OP'}=2\overrightarrow{OF}-\overrightarrow{OP}$.

### Solution

Normal $\mathbf n=(2,-1,2)$. The line through $P$: $(2+2t,\ 3-t,\ -1+2t)$. Substitute: $2(2+2t)-(3-t)+2(-1+2t)=-10$, i.e. $-1+9t=-10$, so $t=-1$ and $F=(0,4,-3)$. Check: $0-4-6=-10$.

$\overrightarrow{OP'}=2\overrightarrow{OF}-\overrightarrow{OP}=(0,8,-6)-(2,3,-1)=(-2,5,-5)$, i.e. $P'=(-2,5,-5)$. Check: $\overrightarrow{PF}=(-2,1,-2)$ has length $3$ and $FP'=(-2,1,-2)$ as well, and $2(-2)-5+2(-5)=-19$ lies the same distance $9$ on the other side of the plane value $-10$.
